# Task

Review the supplied path for runtime reliability using its stated contract. Explain any supported causal issue, justified protection, or missing context. Keep claims bounded to visible evidence.

# RT-43: supplied context

This is one synthetic request starting at logical time 0. Its total lifetime, including setup and work, is 100 logical units. The supplied ManualClock is the scheduler; its schedule rejects negative or nonfinite delays and no other scheduling failure is assumed. On total deadline or parent abort, owned phases, timers and listeners must be released. Normal defaults are setupDuration=80 and workDuration=60. Zero-duration phases are allowed. At exactly 100 the deadline wins over phase success because it is armed first. Counters model owned work, not real sockets, traffic or production load.
The accepted input domain and invalid-input rejection/cleanup policy are not supplied. No upstream validator is shown; its existence or absence must not be assumed.

The supplied path enforces the stated total deadline for valid phase durations. I found no supported deadline or cancellation defect in that path.

[handleRequest](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-EbpFEm/repo/RT-43/service.mjs:3) forces a 100-unit timeout and disables resetting it after setup. With the defaults, setup finishes at 80, work starts, and the deadline finishes the request as `timed-out` at 100. The shared [finish function](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-EbpFEm/repo/shared/deadline-stages.mjs:10) cancels the current phase and deadline, removes the abort listener, and clears the active-work counter. An already-aborted parent starts no phase; a later abort uses the same cleanup.

The deadline is scheduled before setup. The [clock](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-EbpFEm/repo/shared/clock.mjs:17) resolves equal-time timers in scheduling order, so the deadline wins at exactly 100, including when zero-duration phases are involved.

There is an **input-policy uncertainty**: a negative or nonfinite setup duration makes scheduling throw after the deadline and listener have been installed; an invalid work duration throws from the setup callback while the deadline remains armed. The supplied contract does not say whether such durations can reach this function or what cleanup invalid-input rejection requires, so this is not enough to establish a contract violation. That policy and the caller’s validation boundary would be needed to decide whether protection is required.

The review is limited to the supplied files; no test suite or production behavior was assessed.

**Runtime Research (revision 1)**

The supplied path enforces the stated total deadline for scheduled phases. [handleRequest](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-tiSAFv/repo/RT-43/service.mjs:3) fixes the timeout at 100 and disables resetting it after setup. With the default durations, setup finishes at 80 and work would finish at 140, so the deadline finishes the request at 100 and cancels the pending work timer. The deadline is armed first, so it also wins a tie at 100, as required.

[finish](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-tiSAFv/repo/shared/deadline-stages.mjs:10) cancels the owned phase and deadline timers, removes the abort listener, clears the active counter, and resolves the response. A parent abort uses the same cleanup path, including when the signal is already aborted. Zero-duration phases can be scheduled and remain subject to the same deadline ordering.

There is an unresolved input-boundary question. [ManualClock.schedule](/var/folders/kb/clk179sd5qq5htsth48gfk5c0000gn/T/brooks-runtime-study-tiSAFv/repo/shared/clock.mjs:7) throws for negative or nonfinite durations, and the phase scheduling calls do not catch that exception. An invalid setup duration throws after the deadline and abort listener have been installed; an invalid work duration throws from the setup callback while the deadline remains armed. A later deadline or abort can still run cleanup, but the exception itself does not do so. The supplied contract does not define accepted inputs or invalid-input cleanup, and no conclusion about upstream validation is supported. Those details are needed to decide whether this is a defect.

These conclusions concern the synthetic clock and owned-work counters only; they do not establish behavior of real transports, production load, retries, or admission limits.
